subject: Computer Networking
title: The OSI Model
description: A 60-second lesson on The OSI Model.

hook.text: Networking was chaotic in the 1970s. The OSI model tried to organize it into seven clean layers.

buildup.text: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application — each layer has a clear job.

discovery.text: The model helps engineers discuss networking without confusion. Layer 3 means routing. Layer 4 means transport.

twist.text: The OSI protocols themselves never caught on. TCP/IP won in practice. But the model remained as a teaching tool.

climax.text: Every networking textbook, certification, and interview references the OSI model. It's the shared vocabulary.

punchline.text: OSI lost the protocol war but won the education one.

quiz.question: How many layers does the OSI model define?

details.summary: The OSI model, published in 1984, divides network communication into seven layers from physical cabling to user applications. Although the internet uses TCP/IP instead, the OSI model remains the standard framework for teaching and discussing networking concepts, protocols, and troubleshooting.
details.whyItMatters: The OSI model provides a shared vocabulary for discussing network problems and architecture. When engineers say it is a Layer 2 problem, they are using the OSI model.
takeaways: Seven layers from physical to application define network functions
The OSI model is a teaching and discussion framework
TCP/IP maps roughly to the OSI model but with fewer layers

faq.question: Why did the internet adopt TCP/IP instead of OSI?
faq.answer: TCP/IP was already working and widely deployed when the OSI model was published. OSI protocols were complex and slow to implement. TCP/IP had the advantage of being real, tested, and free. Practical adoption always beats theoretical elegance.

faq.question: Why is the OSI model still taught if nobody uses it?
faq.answer: It provides a clean conceptual framework for understanding how networks work. Each layer has a clear responsibility. Troubleshooting is easier when you can identify which layer a problem occurs at. The model is a communication tool, not an implementation specification.
